status: DONE — both repairs are committed in my paths, with builder tests; the named suites are green apart from 9 W1-20 errors the sandbox causes.
work_completed: (1) `gov retrieve` now collects the ids a request names: the id-shaped tokens of the question, each `--id`, and the `--ticket`. The rule is drawn at "every": when every named id is id-shaped and none exists anywhere (no record has it and no line of the lexical index holds it as a whole token), the request stops with `UNRESOLVED_IDS`. Each id is listed as an `UNRESOLVED` gap, with no evidence, `continuation: null` and one empty batch. If even one named id exists, the request is answered as before, and the closure still lists the missing ids as gaps beside the answer. It is also answered as before when an `--id` is not id-shaped (a symbol name, which the closure asks the code index about), when `--continue` is given, or when the index or the record graph cannot be read. The rule is written in the module docstring. (2) An `sqlite3.DatabaseError` raised inside `retrieve()` now becomes `GovError("STORE_UNREADABLE", …)`, with the root and the error in its details. The CLI puts it in the command's envelope with exit 1, as it does `STORE_MISSING`, and prints no traceback. It can only fire when `retrieve` has already raised and no bundle exists, so it never hides a real answer. The docstring's exit-code list names it.

discoveries: The CLI turns any `GovError` raised by a command into the envelope with exit 1, whatever its code, so `STORE_UNREADABLE` needed no declaration in the command module.
risks: (1) A missing `--ticket` that is id-shaped now gets the stated gap (`UNRESOLVED_IDS`) instead of retrieve's behaviour. W1-21's ticket case accepts that outcome and still passes. (2) The `UTF-8` false-positive risk from my first return still stands: any id-shaped token that no file holds triggers the gap. (3) `STORE_UNREADABLE` also catches other `sqlite3.DatabaseError`s from `retrieve`, a locked store for example. Those raised before as well, so the change only gives them a code and an envelope.
lessons: A test of the CLI path can call `gov.cli.main.main([...])` with `capsys`. To check the envelope, look for the code in stdout and for no "Traceback" in stderr.
